To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the WCD is a temporary device for the protection of patients with a high risk of sudden cardiac arrest and that bipolar stimulation may result in double counting of the detection algorithm and should be avoided.
The wearable cardioverter defibilator (WCD) can be used in pacemaker-dependent patients.
the use of a WCD is safe and effective for patients at high risk of sudden death and that it can be used as a bridge to permanent implantable cardioverter defibrillators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a wearable cardioverter defibrillators.
the development of a new method for the determination of the optimal parameters of a WCD system for the detection of ventricular fibrillation.
the development and evaluation of a new algorithm for the detection of cardiac arrhythmias in the context of wearable cardioverter defib- rillator (WCD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a WCD is not recommended in patients with a permanent pacemaker.
the use of a WCD is not recommended in a pacemakers-dependent patient with a high risk of sudden cardiac arrest, but in case of an indication, it should be used only with a monopolar configuration.
the use of a WCD in a pacemakers patient is possible but should be done with caution and with the knowledge of possible pitfalls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the importance of the correct programming of the WCD in patients with a pacemaker and the need for further studies to evaluate the safety of the WCD algorithm in pacemaker-dependent patients.
the WCD is a safe and effective method of sudden cardiac death prevention in patients with reversible arrhythmic conditions.
the WCD should be programmed to a single-chamber mode and the pacemaker should be programmed to bipolar pacing mode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WCD should be used only in monopolar stimulation patients or patients with a single-chamber device.
the WCD should not be worn in a pacemakers-dependent patient if bipolar pacing is used.
the WCD should not be used during bipolar ventricular pacing.
